builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted assistant is too expensive because its model uses most of the GPU memory.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's supported lower-precision weights on a copy of your serving setup.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model at its original precision, on the same GPU.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak memory, task pass rate, latency, and total serving cost at the same context and load.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Practical Semantic Communication for General-Purpose Networks: Compression of High-Dimensional Embeddings Under Quantization
summary: Replaces task-agnostic scalar/vector quantization of embeddings with a learned compression matrix optimized under a relaxed Gaussian Information Bottleneck objective with closed-form gradients. Costs: an offline training/optimization step per task and embedding type, plus channel-model assumptions; compute is modest but requires task labels or a target variable. Can fail when the channel model or noise statistics are misestimated, when the downstream task shifts (the compression is task-specific), or on non-text modalities not validated in the paper.
rationale: The method is small-scale and cheap enough to implement on a single GPU, but its benefit depends on the reader actually transmitting embeddings over constrained channels and on task-specific retraining, so workload-specific validation is required before adoption.
technique: Task-aware embedding compression via relaxed GIB

claims.statement: Replaces task-agnostic scalar/vector quantization of embeddings with a learned compression matrix optimized under a relaxed Gaussian Information Bottleneck objective with closed-form gradients. Costs: an offline training/optimization step per task and embedding type, plus channel-model assumptions; compute is modest but requires task labels or a target variable. Can fail when the channel model or noise statistics are misestimated, when the downstream task shifts (the compression is task-specific), or on non-text modalities not validated in the paper.

Outperforms task-agnostic quantization-based compression, maintaining high semantic fidelity at low bit budgets per embedding on text classification tasks; no multiplicative factor is stated in the abstract.
